issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template Main.java expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() returning a String (the spec shows messageOnRide():String and example usage in Main calls r.messageOnRide()). However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) implement messageOnRide(int speed). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion: students following the template/problem will attempt to call messageOnRide() with no arguments, but the provided solution API requires an int parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable.messageOnRide signature across all artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem statement and template: change the Rideable interface in the solution to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an int speed parameter is desired, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main.java to reflect messageOnRide(int speed) and update calls accordingly.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified without parameters in the problem statement and the template Main expects a no-argument call (messageOnRide()). However, the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements the ride message using the speed parameter and an altered return format (e.g. "Riding on Pig [name] at [speed] mph"). This mismatch in method signature and expected return content creates a mapping barrier: students reading the problem and template will implement/use a no-arg messageOnRide() that returns "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", while the solution uses a different signature and message format.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Rideable API across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Rideable.messageOnRide(int) -> Rideable.messageOnRide() and modify Pig and Seal implementations to return exactly "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and update expected output examples to include the speed phrase (e.g. "Riding on Pig [name] at [speed] mph"). Option A is recommended to preserve the original no-argument specification in the exercise.
